🇮🇷 Iran rolls out new tools to tighten control over Strait of Hormuz
Iran's military is using new systems to better monitor the strait, Press TV reports, citing Iran’s Army spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia.
Vessels attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz must do so in coordination with the Iranian authorities, as those who fail to do so face considerable risks, Akramnia warned.
He added that the measures implemented by Iran allowed it to foil the plans of its enemies who merely use nuclear and missile issues as pretexts for pursuing other, hidden objectives.
This week alone, at least three tankers that attempted to pass the strait while skirting the rules set by Iran ended up suffering explosions and catching fire after striking mines.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇸🇦🇾🇪 Saudi Arabia amasses thousands of foreign troops – will they attack Yemen?
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) is likely to use his attendance at the G20 summit in Miami to personally appeal to US President Donald Trump for military assistance, Semafor reports, citing a US official familiar with the prince's travel plans.
MSB has already formed a multinational coalition, as regional and European allies pledge military assistance to Riyadh. However, many of them seem reluctant to participate in offensive operations in Yemen.
🟥 Sudan: The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have reportedly pledged to send 10,000 fighters to Saudi Arabia over 18 months. More than 7,000, including around 2,000 Sudan Shield Forces (SSF), [may have already arrived](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77696) 
🟥 Syria: Damascus could send 3,000–20,000 fighters, according to reports, but officials have confirmed only 600 special forces personnel for training and [military consultations ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77907)
🟥 Egypt: Cairo pledged military support in late October, although forces had reportedly already been deployed around Jeddah, Taif and Yanbu. The contingent reportedly includes Rafale fighter jets, eight helicopters, four transport aircraft and 500 specialists, with plans to expand to 1,500 troops. Egyptian warships have also moved closer to the [Bab al-Mandab Strait ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76980)
🟥 Turkey: Ankara has maintained technical teams, air defense systems and electronic warfare equipment in Saudi Arabia since 2025. Further deployments of troops, special forces and aircraft have been reportedly discussed following ratification of the trilateral Mecca Pact. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on November 21 that assistance was forthcoming, but no decision had been made on deploying troops to Yemen.
🟥 Pakistan: Under a 2025 bilateral agreement, Islamabad maintains around 8,000 troops, 16 fighter jets, two drone units and a long-range air defense battery in Saudi Arabia. Pakistan has pledged to counter Houthi attacks but ruled out ground operations in Yemen
🟥 France: Paris reportedly began deploying troops, radars and air defense systems to Yanbu, a Saudi port on the Red Sea coast, around October 13 in exchange for diesel supplies. Some 2,000 French troops are presently stationed across the Gulf, including in Qatar, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia
🟥 Greece: Athens has operated a Patriot battery protecting Saudi energy infrastructure in Yanbu since 2021
🟥 United Kingdom: London has deployed RAF Typhoon fighters to protect Saudi oil infrastructure while ruling out offensive strikes against the Houthis. British refueling aircraft have nevertheless supported Saudi airstrikes in Yemen
The multinational coalition suggests that the Saudi-Yemeni conflict is increasingly extending beyond the Middle East, drawing in African and European powers. It remains unclear whether the US will join MBS's coalition against Yemen as Washington pursues its operations to blockade Iran. Riyadh's regional Muslim allies also appear reluctant to engage Ansar Allah in direct combat.
